description: This bar chart illustrates the relationship between sparsity rate and perplexity, displaying results for “Per-Output” and “Per-Layer” metrics. The horizontal axis represents “Sparsity Rate” with categories labeled 10%, 20%, 30%, 40%, 50%, 60%, 70%, and 80%, arranged in ascending order. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and utilizes a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10⁰ to 10³ with tick labels at powers of 10. For each sparsity rate, there are two adjacent bars: a blue bar representing “Per-Output” and an orange bar representing “Per-Layer.” At 10% sparsity, the blue bar reaches a height of approximately 2, and the orange bar reaches a height of approximately 3. As the sparsity rate increases, the bar heights generally increase, with the 80% sparsity rate showing the blue "Per-Output" bar at approximately 900 and the orange "Per-Layer" bar exceeding 1000. The bars are not visually emphasized, outlined, or annotated in any specific way.
